note: eye boxes per artwork file, as fractions of the measured body box; y is from the top. Each box bounds the eye opening itself — lash to lower lid — because that is what a blink collapses onto. A zero-width box means that eye is not visible in this artwork (a fringe covers it), and the shader skips it rather than dragging the hair down.
blinkNote: Artwork files whose eye boxes have been checked against the artwork, by rendering the blink and looking at it, and are accurate enough to warp with. The blink collapses everything inside the box onto a lid line, so a box that sits beside the eye rather than on it drags the fringe down instead of closing anything — and the boxes here were originally measured for an earlier blinking attempt that drew a shape over the eye rather than moving it, so several of them sat beside the eye by most of a box width. A file belongs here only after its own blink has been looked at; the portraits are all `still` and never rig, so none of them are listed. `yuno-chibi-2.png` is deliberately absent: it is the same look turned to the side, its face sits at the very edge of the body box, and the client only ever rigs the first frame of a look anyway.
